market_definition: Global English-speaking history and archaeology audience, prioritizing practical overlap across North America, the UK, and Europe.
replace_when: Channel-specific YouTube Analytics evidence (viewer geography, audience-online day/time, CTR, impressions, watch-time-by-region) becomes available in sufficient volume to support a channel-specific decision. See metrics_for_evaluation below for exactly what unblocks a replacement.
rationale: External large-sample benchmark evidence favors Sunday morning in US Eastern Time for long-form documentary/educational content. Sunday 14:00 UTC also reaches the UK and Europe during afternoon viewing hours, giving practical overlap across the three target regions without over-optimizing for any single one. Shorts use separate evening-oriented distribution windows and are spread across the week (Monday/Wednesday/Friday) to sustain discovery for the published main episode between long-form releases. Friday receives the final Short because Friday evening is the strongest general Shorts benchmark. This is a provisional experiment, not a permanent optimum -- it has zero Hypogeum-specific analytics backing it (channel has one published episode, <200 lifetime views, no geography/device/time-of-day data ever captured).
known_gaps: platform_analytics table has no geography/device/time-of-day columns today -- these metrics cannot be measured with the current schema; recording this is a later feedback-loop dependency, not implemented in this slice.
ctr and impressions are null in every existing platform_analytics row -- the current YouTube Analytics sync never populated them.

Deliverable-specific schedule keys ('main_episode', 'short_001'/'short_002'/'short_003') match hypogeum.agents.publishing_agent._deliverable_id_for()'s already-established, channel-agnostic convention (f"short_{short_id}") and are the exact real values verified against ep_f3619022's own sealed publishing_record_ep_f3619022.json / publish_calendar.short_id -- not an invented scheme. A channel with a different bundle shape would use different keys -- Factory Core assigns no meaning to these strings.

v1.0.0's flat deliverable_schedule computed every deliverable's next occurrence independently from wall-clock 'now', which could schedule a Short before its own main episode when activation happened shortly after the main's weekly slot (e.g. any time between Sunday 14:00 and the following Monday 18:00). v1.1.0 adds bundle_cycle_policy, which hypogeum.publishing.schedule_compiler now consults FIRST and which anchors every Short's slot to the main episode's own resolved occurrence, not to wall-clock 'now' independently -- this closes that gap. deliverable_schedule is retained for backward-compat/documentation purposes only; installation should use bundle_cycle_policy going forward.
installation: NOT applied to any database. To install (idempotent, preserves every other existing field -- see hypogeum.channel_config.update_channel_operations_profile()): update_channel_operations_profile(channel_id='hypogeum', bundle_cycle_policy=<this file's 'bundle_cycle_policy' object>). Requires explicit operator approval -- not performed by this artifact's presence alone.
